obligation: USCG Cybersecurity in the Marine Transportation System final rule
basis: Applies to owners and operators of vessels, facilities and OCS facilities required to have a security plan under 33 CFR parts 104, 105 and 106 (33 CFR 101.605). The company operates one onshore field and owns no vessel, waterfront facility or OCS facility

citation: TSA SD Pipeline-2021-02G, issued under 49 U.S.C. 114
basis: Applies to owners and operators of hazardous liquid and natural gas pipelines or LNG facilities notified by TSA. The company operates no pipeline: crude is sold at the lease and hauled in the purchaser's tank trucks, associated gas is used as lease fuel, and no TSA notice is on file

Not a final rule. As proposed (226.2), the company is below the SBA size standard for NAICS 211120 (1,250 employees; 13 CFR 121.201) with 7 employees and meets no sector criterion (no MTSA or OCS facility, no TSA-designated pipeline); tracked for planning

The company holds names with Social Security and bank account numbers of royalty owners (about 90 in Florida) and Social Security, driver license and health plan numbers of 7 employees. Subsections (2), (4) and (6) apply; (3) and (5) are not triggered at this size (fewer than 500 Floridians; no notice of more than 1,000 individuals at once); (8) does not apply because the company has no consumer customers

Part 195 does not apply to transportation through onshore production facilities, including flow lines, or by tank truck. The company's piping is production facility piping and flow lines, and crude leaves by the purchaser's tank trucks

Onshore gathering is outside Part 192 unless it is a regulated onshore gathering line, and gathering cannot begin upstream of the end of the production operation. Associated gas is used as lease fuel in the heater-treater and never leaves the production operation
An oil discharge that reaches water must be reported to the National Response Center at once. Relevant where a SCADA failure or attack leads to a release

obligation: NIST CSF 2.0 with NIST SP 800-82 Rev. 3
basis: No binding federal sector cybersecurity rule applies (rows above). The larger partner's questionnaire follows the CSF, and the insurer's application asks about the same practices; adopted as the company's benchmark
About 50 royalty owners live in states other than Florida; the law of each state where affected individuals reside applies, confirmed by counsel at the time of an incident
The policy requires prompt notice and use of panel vendors; the application stated MFA on remote access and offline backups

obligation: Joint operating agreements, crude purchase contract and seismic data license
basis: The seismic license limits access to named users and asks for a statement of access controls at renewal; partners and the purchaser rely on the company as operator
No EAR-controlled technology identified; the company buys commercial well equipment
No SSI held: the company has no MTSA facility or TSA-designated pipeline security plan

obligation: Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (contractual)
basis: Payment cards are not accepted; no card merchant agreement; crude is sold to the purchaser under contract
